airport: Airports show long, straight runways with distinct markings, connected to large terminal buildings, hangars, and aircraft parking stands. They differ from viaducts by being ground-level aviation infrastructure rather than elevated road structures; industrial areas show factories and smokestacks rather than aviation facilities; rivers show water channels without any airport infrastructure.
beach: Beaches appear as sandy or pebbly shorelines along water bodies, with light colors, wave patterns, and occasional beach umbrellas. They contrast with commercial areas by having natural sand rather than retail buildings; deserts show inland sand dunes without water adjacency; mountains show elevated rocky terrain rather than coastal sand.
bridge: Bridges show elevated roadway or railway structures spanning over water or valleys, with visible pillars, deck, and approach ramps. They differ from viaducts by spanning over water rather than land with multiple supports; industrial areas show factories and smokestacks rather than bridge structures; rivers show water channels without any crossing infrastructure.
commercial: Commercial areas show dense retail and office buildings with large parking lots, wide streets, and visible storefronts. They contrast with residential areas by having commercial buildings rather than housing units; beaches show natural sand rather than retail blocks; parking lots show open vehicle storage without any buildings.
desert: Deserts show vast, barren landscapes with sand dunes, rocky outcrops, and sparse dry vegetation, with uniform light tones. They contrast with farmland by lacking crop rows and irrigation; mountains show elevated rocky peaks rather than flat sandy terrain; beaches show coastal sandy areas adjacent to water.
farmland: Farmland appears as large, open agricultural fields with uniform crop rows, regular field boundaries, and occasional irrigation. It differs from desert by having organized crops and vegetation rather than sand; meadow shows natural grassland without field lines; beaches show sandy shoreline rather than agricultural fields.
footballfield: Football fields show rectangular grassy areas with clear boundary lines, goal zones, and often surrounding tracks. They contrast with meadow by having sports markings and maintained grass rather than natural vegetation; parks have walking paths and trees rather than field markings; commercial areas show buildings and parking rather than sports fields.
forest: Forests show dense tree canopy with dark green textures, irregular edges, and no visible ground, often covering large areas. They contrast with ponds by having dense vegetation rather than water features; airports show runways and terminals rather than tree cover; meadows show open grass without tree canopy.
industrial: Industrial areas feature large warehouses, factories, smokestacks, and extensive parking lots with regular blocky layouts. They differ from residential areas by having industrial buildings rather than housing units; bridges show crossing structures rather than factories; commercial areas show retail buildings rather than industrial structures.
meadow: Meadows show open, grassy areas with smooth, uniform texture, often with scattered trees or shrubs, and no field lines. They contrast with farmland by lacking organized crop rows and field boundaries; football fields have sports markings rather than natural grass; deserts show sand rather than grass cover.
mountain: Mountains show elevated, rugged terrain with steep slopes, rocky outcrops, and shadow patterns, often with forested lower elevations. They contrast with deserts by having rocky peaks rather than sand dunes; beaches show coastal sandy areas rather than mountainous terrain; forests show tree cover without exposed rock.
park: Parks show green open spaces with trees, walking paths, ponds, and recreational areas, often irregular in shape. They differ from ponds by being larger areas with vegetation and paths rather than just water; commercial areas show buildings and parking rather than parkland; football fields have sports markings rather than recreational paths.
parking: Parking lots appear as flat, paved areas with rows of vehicles, clear lane markings, and entrance points. They differ from commercial areas by having vehicle storage rather than buildings; industrial areas have warehouses alongside parking rather than just open lots; viaducts show elevated road structures rather than ground-level parking.
pond: Ponds appear as small, circular or irregular water bodies with calm surfaces, often surrounded by vegetation. They contrast with rivers by being still, enclosed water rather than flowing channels; parks are larger green areas with paths and trees rather than just water; forests show tree cover without water features.
port: Ports show waterfront areas with docks, piers, ships, cranes, and large storage areas adjacent to water. They differ from rivers by having docks and ships rather than natural water channels; residential areas show housing units rather than waterfront infrastructure; ponds are small inland water bodies without port facilities.
railwaystation: Railway stations show tracks, platforms, passenger buildings, and surrounding parking lots, often with linear rail lines. They contrast with viaducts by being ground-level stations with platforms rather than elevated rail structures; industrial areas show factories rather than passenger buildings; commercial areas show retail rather than station facilities.
residential: Residential areas show housing units with visible roofs, yards, driveways, and street networks, with varied lot sizes. They differ from industrial areas by having housing rather than factories; commercial areas show retail buildings rather than homes; ports show waterfront infrastructure rather than residential neighborhoods.
river: Rivers appear as narrow, sinuous, dark water channels with flowing patterns and riparian vegetation along banks. They contrast with ponds by being elongated flowing water rather than still enclosed water bodies; beaches show sandy shorelines along water rather than the water channels themselves; bridges are structures spanning across rivers.
viaduct: Viaducts show elevated road or rail structures with long continuous sections and multiple supports, often crossing over land. They differ from bridges by spanning over land rather than water; railway stations are ground-level with tracks and platforms rather than elevated structures; airports show ground-level aviation facilities rather than elevated roads.
